ruling.recommended_action: Refund $7.06 of the excess distance charge to the rider (voucher, NS-7) and retain the remaining $0.47 of the billed excess; no account action.
ruling.reasoning:
RydeTAXI trip, so the fare follows the meter and detour km enter the charge [F6][RD-2]. One off-route segment exists: 09:13–09:24, 6.58 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.57 km, +5.01 km [F3][RD-1]. The rider filed that the driver "never asked me"; there is no in-app chat at all [F7]. Under RD-5 consent must be the rider's own message sent before the segment; the driver's after-the-trip statement that AYE "was crawling and flooding … so I went round it" is not rider consent, and a complete chat record with no rider agreement means the segment counts [F7][F8][RD-5].

The driver's reasonable-cause defence fails on the record. RD-4(b) speed-band evidence alone does not exempt — the trace marks RD-4(a) ✗ (no qualifying incident; F12 confirms none recorded) [F9][F12][RD-4]. The AYE band-2 record (10–19 km/h, 08:49–09:13) stops at 09:13, exactly when the detour begins, so it does not even cover the segment window [F3][F9][RD-4]. Weather is not a listed RD-4 ground [F13][RD-4].

RD-3 needs a rider-named place; the rider named none and no stop was measured [F7][RD-3]. Nothing in the record ties the driven path to any rider-agreed road, so RD-5 can only be read as counting this segment — the absence of chat is a complete record showing no agreement, which settles the finding; no recital of undetermined is needed [F3][F7][RD-5].

Amount: this trip's per-km rate = distance fare ÷ distance km = $22.50 ÷ 15.96 km = $1.4098/km [F6][F4][RD-2]. Non-exempt extra km = 5.01 km [F3]. 5.01 km × $1.4098/km = $7.0629 → $7.06 [F3][F6][F4][RD-2]. The fare's own recital of excess ($7.53 for 5.34 km) is not used because the corridor allowance between the fare's excess km and the measured segment km is not refundable under RD-2 [F4][F3][RD-2]. So 5.01 km is refunded, not 5.34 km: the rider does not get the $0.47 difference [F4][F3][RD-2]. RD-6 is not triggered: route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, and profile facts cannot alone found a breach [F15][RD-6]. Full refund requested by the rider is rejected: only the measured, non-exempt metre units are refundable [F1][F3][RD-2].

RD-3 does not apply — the rider named no place and no stop was measured [F7][RD-3]. The driver's traffic defence fails: the trace marks RD-4(a) ✗ (no incident; F12), and the AYE band-2 record ends at 09:13 when the segment starts, so it does not cover the segment [F9][F12][RD-4]. The segment's 5.01 extra km therefore count, and the whole way is refundable metre units [F3][RD-1][RD-2].

The driver's claim that the AYE trip was excused by flooding/congestion rests only on his after-trip statement [F8]; RD-4 requires an incident fact before the segment (trace ✗, F12) and band evidence alone does not exempt — the AYE band-2 record ends at 09:13 as the segment begins [F9][F12][RD-4], and weather is not an RD-4 ground [F13][RD-4].

Any claim of rider agreement/blessing of the route fails: the chat record is empty [F7] and RD-5 requires a rider message sent before 09:13; a driver's verbal-agreement claim is not consent [F8][F7][RD-5].
